subsystems.name: Feedstock conditioning
subsystems.role: supplies the raw elements — carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen — in pure enough form not to poison the catalysts downstream.
parts: CO2 capture from air or flue gas

subsystems.name: Electrochemical stage
subsystems.role: uses electricity to split water into hydrogen and to reduce carbon dioxide into simple reactive molecules such as formate, methanol or acetate.

subsystems.name: Carbon-fixing cascade
subsystems.role: builds those one- and two-carbon molecules up into the small units food is made of: three- and six-carbon sugars, amino acids and fatty acids.

subsystems.name: Polymerisation and assembly
subsystems.role: links those units into the large molecules we actually eat — starch, protein chains, triglycerides.

subsystems.name: Structuring and formulation
subsystems.role: gives the molecules the water content, texture, mouthfeel and flavour of recognisable food.

subsystems.name: Sensing and control
subsystems.role: keeps a large network of reactors in balance; living and enzymatic systems drift.

buildSteps.title: Capture and purify the feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Pull carbon dioxide from air or a concentrated waste stream and clean it; filter and deionise water; separate nitrogen from air.

buildSteps.title: Make hydrogen and reduced carbon
buildSteps.detail: Run electrolysers to split water, then feed hydrogen and carbon dioxide into cells that reduce the carbon to formate, methanol or acetate.

buildSteps.title: Fix carbon into small molecules
buildSteps.detail: Pass those feedstocks through immobilised enzymes or engineered microbes that assemble them into sugars and organic acids.

buildSteps.title: Build the monomers
buildSteps.detail: Produce amino acids, fatty acids and simple sugars in separate, controlled streams — this is where precision fermentation already works today.

buildSteps.title: Link them into food polymers
buildSteps.detail: Enzymes extend the monomers into starch chains, protein sequences and fats, with chain length and structure tightly controlled.

buildSteps.title: Form the food
buildSteps.detail: Blend, hydrate and texture the output into a stable product — this step, not the chemistry, decides whether people will eat it.

buildSteps.title: Verify safety and nutrition
buildSteps.detail: Test for contaminants, allergens, digestibility and full nutrient content before any release.

buildSteps.title: Scale in modular plants
buildSteps.detail: Replicate reactor modules rather than building one huge plant, so capacity grows with demand.

prerequisites.why: the whole route is energy-hungry — it buys land and water savings with electrons, not with free energy.
labs make formate, methanol and acetate, but not yet cheaply or durably at industrial scale.
CO2 has been converted to starch in the laboratory by enzyme cascades, but slowly and at tiny yields.
it already makes specific proteins and fats commercially, and is the realistic foundation this idea would build on.
no general-purpose machine places individual atoms into food molecules; the 'assembler' part of this idea is theoretical.
food needs nitrogen, and today it comes mainly from very energy-intensive ammonia synthesis.

pathway.milestone: precision fermentation and gas fermentation supply individual ingredients — proteins, fats, flavour molecules
pathway.unlocks: a working industrial base of bioreactors, enzymes and food-safety regulation.

pathway.milestone: cell-free cascades turn carbon dioxide into sugars and starch at useful rates and yields
pathway.unlocks: bulk calories made without farmland for the first time.

pathway.milestone: hybrid plants chain electrolysis, enzymatic synthesis and structuring into one continuous process
pathway.unlocks: food production decoupled from weather, season and arable land.

pathway.milestone: modular, highly automated plants, and only much later any atom-by-atom assembly
pathway.unlocks: regional food security in places that cannot farm — provided the energy and the biology both deliver.
